raw_case_text:
A 76-year-old female presented with painful swelling in the left lateral neck region for 15 days. There was no erythema or heating sensation on neck area, and she had no symptoms of fever. Ten months earlier, she had undergone total thyroidectomy with central neck lymph node dissection due to PTC (T3N1aM0 by American Joint Committee on Cancer/International Union against Cancer Staging System 7th Edition), followed by radioactive iodine therapy and maintenance treatment with levothyroxine.
Thyroid function tests showed mildly suppressed thyrotropin-stimulating hormone (TSH; 0.01 mIU/L; normal range, 0.27-4.2 mIU/L) and elevated free thyroxine (fT4; 2.12 ng/dL; normal range, 0.93-1.70 ng/dL) concentrations. Her white blood cell and neutrophil counts were normal. No pathogens were cultured from her blood, stool, urine, or sputum.
Neck ultrasonography revealed a large heterogeneous echoic (cystic) mass in the left lateral neck (Figure 1) and computed tomography revealed a 3.3 x 5.6 cm sized thick-walled cystic lesion along left levels II, III, and IV (Figure 2). Cytologic examination of the dark brown colored fluid collected from the lesion by fine-needle aspiration showed many neutrophils and macrophages in necrotic background, but there was no evidence of malignancy (Figure 3). However, the mass was suspected of being a metastatic lymph node and was resected.
Intraoperative examination showed that mass was encapsulated and very highly adhesive to the internal jugular vein and around the tissue. There were no other abnormally enlarged lymph nodes. The mass contained dark brown colored fluid and some debris. Microscopic examination of the lymph node mass showed massive necrosis and immunohistochemistry clearly showed that the mass was a metastatic papillary carcinoma (Figure 4). Culture of the fluid showed the presence of Salmonella Typhi.
No postoperative complications occurred. The patient was treated with intravenous cephalosporin for 6 days; following antibiotic sensitivity testing of the cultured Salmonella Typhi, she was switched to oral ciprofloxacin for 7 days. Regular follow-up examinations have shown no evidence of additional metastasis, recurrence of metastasis, or residual infection.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 76-year-old female with a history of papillary thyroid carcinoma presented with a 15-day history of painful swelling in the left lateral neck.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed a painful mass in the left lateral neck over 15 days without fever, overlying skin erythema, or local warmth.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC, stage T3N1aM0) treated 10 months earlier with total thyroidectomy and central neck lymph node dissection, followed by radioactive iodine ablation and suppressive levothyroxine therapy.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for painful left lateral neck swelling. Pertinent negatives: no fever, neck erythema, or local warmth. Home medication: levothyroxine.

objective.physical_examination: Left lateral neck swelling without overlying erythema or warmth; afebrile.
objective.routine_investigations: Thyroid function tests on levothyroxine suppression showed mildly suppressed TSH (0.01 mIU/L; normal: 0.27-4.2 mIU/L) and elevated free T4 (2.12 ng/dL; normal: 0.93-1.70 ng/dL). White blood cell and neutrophil counts were normal. Blood, stool, urine, and sputum cultures were negative. Neck ultrasonography demonstrated a large heterogeneous cystic mass in the left lateral neck.
objective.advanced_workup: Neck CT revealed a 3.3 x 5.6 cm thick-walled cystic lesion extending along left cervical levels II, III, and IV. Fine-needle aspiration (FNA) yielded dark-brown fluid containing abundant neutrophils and macrophages on a necrotic background without overt malignant cells on cytology. Surgical excision of the encapsulated mass (which was densely adherent to the internal jugular vein) revealed extensive necrosis with immunohistochemical confirmation of metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma, while bacterial culture of the cystic fluid isolated Salmonella Typhi.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Cystic lateral neck lymph node metastasis of papillary thyroid carcinoma secondarily infected with Salmonella Typhi, confirmed by surgical histopathology/immunohistochemistry and aspirate fluid bacterial culture growing S. Typhi (with negative blood, urine, stool, and sputum cultures). Following complete surgical resection of the infected metastatic lymph node without postoperative complications, the patient received intravenous cephalosporin therapy for 6 days followed by a 7-day course of oral ciprofloxacin guided by antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Regular follow-up showed no recurrence of infection or further thyroid cancer metastasis.
